column3: Immediate antecedent: the word has become binding on those who do not believe.
Names the messenger's warning role, but adds no receptive-recipient or verdict dynamic.
The creative divine command is not about warning or the response to it.
Shows Allah establishing truth through His words against resistance, a partial parallel to the binding word.
Identifies the Quran that the surrounding passage presents as the vehicle of warning.
Generic reported speech does not clarify warning, life, or the binding verdict.
Supplies the difficult consequence borne by disbelievers after the warning is refused.
Immediate context: the message is a clear remembrance and Quran, not poetry.
Truth and misguidance are contrasted without the warning-recipient or verdict sequence.
Pairs the erasure of falsehood with Allah's establishment of truth by His words.
A historical warning-and-punishment example, but it is less specific than the closer parallels.
Places the present warner in continuity with earlier warnings.

An exact parallel in which the word becomes binding upon prior communities.

Rules about public evil speech are unrelated to warning efficacy or the verdict.

The demand for an accompanying angel warner exposes resistance to the messenger's existing warning role.

Demanding the timing of the promise is a secondary form of resisting warning.

Immediate context identifies the community's reaction to reminder as culpable excess.

Death brings the avoided truth as an unavoidable event, completing the focus's warning horizon.
Feeding during famine does not address warning, life, or disbelief here.

Immediate setup: the Quran warns a heedless people whose forebears were not warned.
The imposed restraints make visible the closed condition behind warning's ineffectiveness.
Barriers before and behind them explain why signs and warning are not seen.
Allah gives life to the dead and records deeds, directly joining life with accountable outcome.
The believing man runs from the city's edge to urge his people to follow the messengers.
It states the practical response sought from a receptive hearer: follow guided messengers.
The man's declared faith supplies a concrete contrary response to the city's rejection.
Entry into Paradise shows the favorable outcome of responding in faith.
Forgiveness and honor complete the believer's contrasting outcome.
It explicitly laments that people mocked every messenger who came to them.
The destroyed generations provide historical consequence for rejecting messenger warnings.
All people are ultimately brought together before Allah, completing the warning's horizon.
The trumpet summons the dead from graves, clarifying the life beyond death presupposed by the focus.
The raised ask who revived them, directly connecting resurrection with the fulfilled promise of the Merciful.
A single blast gathers everyone before Allah for the decisive encounter.
The day of recompense makes each soul answer for what it did.
The command to separate the criminals displays the final distinction implicit in the binding verdict.
Hell is identified as what the criminals were promised and had denied.
Entry into Hell is explicitly tied to prior disbelief.
Sealed mouths and witnessing limbs make rejected truth and deeds publicly manifest.
The reversal of long life is a secondary biological-life counterpart to the focus's living recipient.
The human objection to revival after death directly tests the warning's resurrection horizon.
The challenge about decayed bones exposes the denial answered by the focus's message.
The One who originated bones will revive them, directly answering the denial of life after death.
The Creator of heavens and earth has power to recreate people.
The divine command that brings a thing into being supports the certainty of resurrection.
Return to Allah gives the final destination toward which warning directs its hearer.
It states that warning and non-warning are alike for those fixed in disbelief.
Sealed hearts, hearing, and sight give a close account of why warning no longer reaches them.
Disbelief in signs leads to abiding in the Fire, supplying the consequence side of the focus.

Messengers who bring glad tidings and warning remove people's excuse before Allah.
The arrival of a messenger after an interval prevents the claim that no bearer of warning came.
Those who hear respond, while the dead are raised by Allah, closely paralleling receptive life and nonresponse.

Those who deny signs and reject them arrogantly are assigned the Fire.
Each community's messenger is followed by judgment in justice.

Warning by revelation reaches those who hear, whereas the deaf do not hear the call when warned.
The Criterion is sent down so that its servant may be a warner to all worlds.

Sending a messenger forestalls the claim that people would have followed signs if warned.
A revealed book warns a people to whom no warner had previously come so that they may be guided.
The messenger is sent to all people as bearer of glad tidings and warner.
The living and dead are not equal, and those in graves cannot be made to hear.
The near Day is announced as a warning before hearts rise to the throats.
A warning modeled on the thunderbolt punishment of earlier peoples gives a concrete threat.

People are commanded to respond to their Lord before an irreversible Day arrives.
